title: Esgridge's POEMS work at Marshall and Alzofon's nucleonic spin

plain: A podcast host called Jack, speaking on a Jesse Michels episode with the Navy scientist Salvatore Pais, lists earlier lines of research. He says a researcher named Richard Esgridge looked into something, which this story calls POEMS, at the Marshall Space Flight Center, a NASA site. He also mentions a man named Alzofon and his approaches based on "nucleonic spin," the spin of particles in the atom's core, which he says Alzofon worked through with the physicist Richard Feynman back in the 1930s, a hint that such unusual physics has a longer history than people think.
